subject: Informal coaching: expectations and checkpoints for Q3
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Informal coaching: expectations and checkpoints for Q3

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for meeting this morning. As discussed, I wanted to put our coaching conversation in writing so we have a shared set of expectations to follow over the next 6 weeks. This is informal documentation intended to clarify outcomes and give you runway to course-correct before we consider formal steps.

What we covered today (high level):
- Areas of concern: turnaround on assigned tickets, missed acceptance criteria on two sprints, and reduced collaboration in weekly planning.
- Impact: delivery predictability for the product squad and extra work for PM/eng leads to clean up PRs.
- Goal: consistent, production-ready deliverables and clearer proactive communication about blockers.

Immediate actions we agreed on:
1) For the next two sprints, prioritize no more than two active stories at a time and ensure definition-of-done checklist is completed before requesting review.
2) Daily standup accountability: call out one clear blocker and an owner for it.
3) Pair with a peer (I suggest Karthik or Marcus) on the most complex ticket each sprint.
4) End-of-week 1 and 3 progress notes to me (email), including blockers and artifacts.

Success criteria (what "good enough" looks like by the end of 6 weeks):
- PRs merged with CI passing and QA signoff within target lead times (>80% of assigned work).
- Fewer reassignments due to incomplete acceptance criteria.
- Clear update in squad planning and fewer surprise high-priority fixes.

I'll keep a record on my side; Laura, copying you to ensure HR has awareness and can advise on documentation. I attached the short notes from our call. If any of the actions feel unclear, say so here and we'll refine.

Attachments:
- performance-notes-June.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 12KB)

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — I appreciate you writing this up. Quick clarifications:

- When you say "no more than two active stories," should I still pick up small bugfixes (<2 hours) outside those stories or keep my focus strictly to the two stories?
- For pairings, I can reach out to Karthik today; should I mark those sessions on my calendar and send you a short note after each pairing?

I'll review the attached notes in detail later today. I want to be transparent: I'm committed to improving and I think the pairing idea will help.

—Neha

> - When you say "no more than two active stories," should I still pick up small bugfixes (<2 hours) outside those stories or keep my focus strictly to the two stories?
> - For pairings, I can reach out to Karthik today; should I mark those sessions on my calendar and send you a short note after each pairing?

Thanks for the quick reply and the attitude here — that's exactly the right approach. To be explicit: small bugfixes under 2 hours are okay to triage between the two primary stories, but please flag any that threaten the sprint goal. Yes, please schedule pairing sessions on the calendar and copy me on the invite; after each session, a one-paragraph note (bullet points are fine) in email to me will be good.

I've converted our informal plan into a short checklist (attached) with checkpoints at week 1, week 3, and week 6. Please treat week 1 as a check-in (does the plan feel achievable?) and week 3 as an escalation point for any persistent blockers. If, by week 6, we haven't seen sustained improvement on the success criteria, we will consider next steps (formal PIP or alternative role matching).

I've also added Jonas here as a leadership FYI so he's aware of the plan and timeline.

Attachments:
- follow-up-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 5KB)

Best,
Marissa
